acceptanceCriteria.statement: PLANCK -> RGB COLOR LAW: given an absolute temperature T (Kelvin), the emission module returns a physically-plausible blackbody color on the Planck locus — visible-band emission is ~zero for cold T (peak in the IR), and as T rises the color moves deep-red -> orange -> white with monotonically increasing visible luminance.

verifyVia.input: Call the Planck->RGB / spectral-radiance function over a T sweep {150, 300, 800, 1100, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3500} K; read the returned RGB + a visible-luminance scalar.
verifyVia.observable: visible luminance is ~0 (below a small epsilon) for T <= ~800 K and strictly increasing for T above the visible threshold; hue progresses red -> orange -> white (R dominates first, G then B rise) with rising T; all outputs finite and in-gamut [0,1] after tonemap.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ABSOLUTE T-FIELD CONSTRUCTION: the writer builds a per-node Kelvin temperature field T(phi, theta_substellar) from T_eq (D1) scaled by an internal-heat factor and the #3a Ward W(phi) insolation shape, plus — for tidally-locked bodies — a substellar dayside term and a nightside floor. For a NON-locked giant the field is the annual-mean latitudinal shape (no substellar hotspot); for a LOCKED body it peaks near the substellar point and never drops below the floor.

verifyVia.input: Run the emission writer for a locked hot-Jupiter driver bundle and for a non-locked Jovian bundle across seeds {1,2,7,42}; read the T field per node + the substellar geometry.
verifyVia.observable: T finite and bounded for every node/seed; locked case: max(T) occurs within a small angular radius of the substellar point AND min(T) >= nightsideFloorK (~1100 K); non-locked case: T is a function of latitude only (no longitudinal hotspot), matching an arm's-length re-derivation from T_eq * heatFactor * W(phi) within 1e-3.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: INVARIANTS + DETERMINISM: the emission writer emits ONLY its own emission channel(s) — it never mutates carrier.height/relief NOR the #3a reflectance/band/turbulence/mushball fields; it contains no Math.random()/Date.now() call form (all randomness alea-seeded off macroSeed, in a disjoint namespace); run twice on the same carrier with the same (regime, macroSeed, drivers) it yields byte-identical emission fields.

verifyVia.input: Snapshot carrier.height + all #3a fields before the emission writer and compare after; static-grep the emission module for /Math\.random\s*\(|Date\.now\s*\(/ (expect zero) and for its alea namespace prefix; run the writer twice per (regime, seed) and compare emission Float32Arrays; re-run the #3a golden bandField hash.
verifyVia.observable: carrier.height + every #3a field byte-identical before/after; zero RNG/clock matches; emission fields byte-identical across the two runs for every (seed, regime); #3a golden bandField hash still -1329854088.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: HOT GLOWS / COLD STAYS DARK: in the lab, the Hot-Jupiter preset renders a visible thermal glow composited additively over the #3a bands (fixing 'hot giant renders cold'), while a cold giant (Jovian) renders no visible added emission (reflectance-only).

verifyVia.input: Open planet-lod-lab.html in the browser; select Hot Jupiter (locked giant) and screenshot; select Gas giant (Jovian) and screenshot; sample emissive contribution in each.
verifyVia.observable: hot-Jupiter shows emissive brightness clearly above zero on the dayside (glows), bands still discernible underneath; Jovian shows ~zero added emission (its look is unchanged from the pre-#2 reflectance render).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: TEMPERATURE -> COLOR SWEEP IS VISIBLE: sweeping the lab T_eq slider up on a giant makes the glow appear and shift red -> orange -> white, tracking the Planck locus.

verifyVia.input: In the lab, on a giant preset, sweep the T_eq slider across low/mid/high values and screenshot each.
verifyVia.observable: at low T_eq no visible glow; increasing T_eq introduces a deep-red glow that brightens and whitens; the on-screen color shift matches the AC1 locus ordering.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: SUBSTELLAR HOTSPOT OFFSET EASTWARD + NIGHTSIDE FLOOR: on a tidally-locked hot-Jupiter, the brightest emission is a dayside hotspot offset EASTWARD of the substellar longitude (advected by the prograde equatorial jet), and the nightside still faintly glows (~1100 K floor), not black.

verifyVia.input: In the lab, render a locked hot-Jupiter with the substellar point at a known longitude; locate the emission-brightness centroid; sample nightside (anti-substellar) emission.
verifyVia.observable: the hotspot brightness centroid longitude is EAST of the substellar longitude by a measurable, non-zero offset; anti-substellar (nightside) emission luminance is > 0 but < dayside peak (floor holds, not pure black).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ADDITIVE COMPOSITOR + #3a REGRESSION: emission composites ADDITIVELY over the #3a reflectance (bands read underneath the glow), and with emission gated OFF (or on a cold body) the lab render is byte-identical to the pre-#2 #3a reflectance path — #2 adds a register, it does not alter the reflectance pipeline.

verifyVia.input: Toggle the emission register off in the lab and compare the render to the #3a baseline (Jovian/Saturnian/Neptunian); confirm bands remain visible under the hot-Jupiter glow when on.
verifyVia.observable: emission-OFF render matches the pre-#2 #3a render for every giant preset (no reflectance drift); with emission ON the underlying bands are still discernible through the additive glow (not overwritten).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: HOLISTIC (Max's gate, never auto-PASSed): the hot-Jupiter reads as a hot, self-luminous world — glowing, with an eastward-offset substellar hotspot, cohesive with the underlying bands — not a cold striped ball wearing a color filter.

verifyVia.input: Max views the Hot-Jupiter preset in the lab (day/night rotation, a T_eq sweep, a re-roll or two) and judges the whole experience.
verifyVia.observable: Max confirms it reads as a genuinely hot, self-luminous giant with a believable hotspot and cohesive bands. Deferred-to-Max; the verify workflow never PASSes this AC.

inputs: #3a climate-e5 fields: the Ward annual-mean insolation W(phi,epsilon) (latitudinal T-shape) and the reflectance/bandNorm the emission composites over (src/worldengine/base/climate-e5.js)

D1 tempEq (equilibrium temperature, Kelvin) — the magnitude of the T-field. LAB: sourced from the regime preset + a lab slider (planet-lod-lab.html DRIVER_PRESETS, existing tempEq ~L2308). GAME (#9): real per-body D1 from PhysicsEngine.equilibriumTemperature
D7 tidal-lock state — selects locked (substellar hotspot geometry) vs non-locked (annual-mean latitudinal) emission mode
#3a equatorial jet direction (eqSign / signed u) — sets the EASTWARD advection direction of the substellar hotspot offset
internalHeat — the internal-heat factor raising effective emitting temperature (v1 = archetype constant per climate-e5.js DRIVER_BUNDLES; seed-variation deferred to the #9 gap per ATMOSPHERE-PLAN §e)
macroSeed — alea seeded off it for any per-seed emission jitter; disjoint namespace from plates/shellRelief/climateE5 (plates.js determinism discipline)
Lab render/compositor seam: planet-lod-height.glsl.js (zonalBandCol reflectance) + planet-lod-uniforms.js — where the additive emission term is blended over reflectance
outputs: A reusable EMISSION REGISTER: per-node emission RGB + intensity (the blackbody-locus color from Planck(T)) as its own channel, additive over reflectance — the compositor reused by #4 (aurora/lightning/airglow), #5 (brown-dwarf self-luminous), #6 (lava rock-vapour glow)
An absolute Kelvin temperature field T(phi, theta_substellar) — substrate reserved for #5/#6 (self-luminous / rock-vapour) and any later thermal read
The substellar-hotspot mask + eastward offset (hot-Jupiter identity tell) — render into the Hot-Jupiter (and hot giant) lab presets; albedo/emissive only, NO relief write
Planck->RGB + T-field construction functions covered by a new emission-e vitest harness (determinism + golden byte snapshot, mirroring climate-e5)
mustStayWorking: #3a bands/jets render UNCHANGED when emission is off / for cold bodies — the golden bandField hash (-1329854088) and every climate-e5 field stay byte-identical; #2 adds a register, never edits the reflectance path
The lab dispatch/build pipeline: buildIrregularSphere -> makeSphereField -> climate-e5 writer -> (new) emission writer -> shader; solid/terrestrial presets keep emission gated to 0 (exact no-op)
Gas-giants-have-no-relief invariant: the emission writer never writes carrier.height / relief channels (verify.js regime constraint)
Existing base-writer tests (plates, shellRelief, climate-e5 AC1-AC9) stay green; the new emission tests are additive
The shipped Earthlike plate dispatch (isEarthlikePlatePath / writePlates) and icy/despun shellRelief path — emission must not alter solid-world dispatch or rendering
